message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑run **gcloud** command that creates a Compute Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
If you prefer the raw REST‑API payload, the JSON snippet is also shown.

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# 1. Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a new VM instance
gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --zone="${ZONE}" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
    --subnet="default" \
    --network-tier="PREMIUM" \
    --maintenance-policy="MIGRATE" \
    --provisioning-model="STANDARD" \
    --service-account="default" \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --boot-disk-device-name="rtx-a6000-ubuntu" \
    --no-shielded-secure-boot \
    --no-shielded-vtpm \
    --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring \
    --reservation-affinity="any" \
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: add a startup script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS base image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a shell script at first boot (e.g., install drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust `count=` and `--machine-type` accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Payload (JSON)

If you’re calling the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., via `curl` or a client library), use the following JSON body:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> Replace `"projects/your-project-id"` with your actual GCP project ID.  
> The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically after the instance boots.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project ID** – set correctly (`PROJECT_ID`).
- [ ] **Zone** – choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).
- [ ] **Machine Type** – ensure it has enough memory for your workload.
- [ ] **GPU Count** – adjust `count=` if you need more than one GPU.
- [ ] **Boot Disk Size** – increase if you plan to store large datasets locally.
- [ ] **Startup Script** – optional but recommended to install GPU drivers automatically.

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

That’s all! Let me know if you’d like help automating this with Terraform, Deployment Manager, or another IaC tool.
